reading.en: MISSING! Our cat Mimi. Mimi is three years old, small and grey. She has green eyes and one white paw. She is very friendly, but she is afraid of dogs. Mimi lives at Husemannstraße 12, fourth floor. She has been gone since Monday. Her favourite food is fish. Have you seen Mimi? Please get in touch: Lena, 0176 23 18 90. Thank you! · Neighbour: Hello, I'm Mr Ziegler, second floor. A grey cat with green eyes? She is in my kitchen. Since Monday. She's eating my fish. · Lena: Mimi! Mr Ziegler, thank you so much! · Mr Ziegler: You're welcome. But I have a question too. Who is Maya? The note is very well written. German isn't her language, is it? · Maya: No. I come from Canada. I've been learning German for twelve weeks. · Mr Ziegler: Twelve weeks! And already a Steckbrief. My English after twelve years of school: “The cat is on the table.” That's all. · Maya: The cat is on the table. I can do that too. · Lena: And under the sofa. And in the bed. And in Mr Ziegler's kitchen.
reading.fact: *Steckbrief* once meant a wanted poster for a criminal. Today it is the word for any profile: a lost cat, a new colleague on the notice board, a pupil on the first day of school.

grammar[0].blocks[1].text: *Lieblingsessen*, *Lieblingsfarbe*, *Lieblingsstadt*, *Lieblingswort*: favourite + the word, one compound, the article of the last word. Mein Lieblingswort ist *Feierabend*.

grammar[0].fact: German school children write a *Steckbrief* about themselves on the first day: name, age, Lieblingstier, Lieblingsessen. A classroom wall in September is forty of them.

grammar[1].fact: You now know about 350 German words, every form of five verbs, and three cases of looking at a noun. A German child reaches this point at about three and a half. You did it in twelve chapters.

document.intro: A real lost-cat notice, pinned to a tree in a village in Baden-Württemberg. You cannot read the small print, so write the notice the way it should be, with the words of this chapter.
document.fact: Lost-cat notices are a German village genre. They are taped to trees, lamp posts and the bakery door, and the cat is usually in a neighbour's garage.
